name: Haʻamonga ʻa Maui
note: Main archaeological landmark; 2 counted sources, 11083 views.

name: Ancient Royal Tombs of Lapaha
note: The langi are the attraction; the Muʻa village entry is dropped as a near-duplicate wrapper (owner brief).

name: Nukuʻalofa
note: Town with its own draws (waterfront, royal sights from outside, markets); the island's base.

name: Hufangalupe
note: Natural sight on the south-east coast.

name: Mapu ʻa Vaea
note: Natural sight on the west-coast route.

name: Anahulu Caves
note: Guided cave swim; Matatahi 'Anahulu Beach rejected as its near-duplicate.

name: Talamahu Market
note: Daily market hall (not a weekly market).

name: Pangaimotu Island
note: Island day trip from Nukuʻalofa; the island is the spot, the boat is the way there.

name: Flying Fox Reserve
note: Roadside wildlife stop (Lonely Planet, Tonga Pocket Guide).

name: Haʻatafu Beach
note: Second-tier beach stop; needs transport.

name: ʻEua National Park
note: Park named by Wikivoyage and Tonga Tourism. Kept as a spot of the ʻEua island destination: 4.5 km2, too small to be a destination beside the island it sits in. Coordinates are the park centre; pin stage must take a visitor point (day-use area, trailhead or main lookout), not the centroid.

name: Rock Gardens
note: Tourism board and Pocket Guide name it; south-coast cluster reached from ʻEua's base. Adjacent to Lakufaʻanga Cliffs (about 200 m) but kept as a separate kept place; pin stage may merge the two into one stop if one pin is wanted.

name: Lakufaʻanga Cliffs
note: Tourism board and Pocket Guide name it; the same south-coast stop as Rock Gardens, kept separately because both were kept.

name: Big Ovava Tree
note: Wikivoyage calls it the park's main attraction; a distinct natural landmark reached by a 3-hour hike.

name: Liʻangahuo ʻa Maui
note: Tourism board and Pocket Guide name it; short walk from the south-coast stops.

name: Haʻaluma Beach
note: Tourism board and Pocket Guide name it as a swim stop. Pin is a Pocket Guide geo tag; pin stage should confirm against OSM natural/beach.

name: ʻOtumatafena Tidal Pools
note: Tourism board highlight; single counted source, kept by the skeptic. Coordinates are an approximate midpoint, so the pin must be resolved.

name: Cathedral Cave
note: Tourism board and Pocket Guide name it; the draw is the cavern itself, reached by dive operator from ʻEua. Dive-only access noted for research.

name: Tofua
note: Kept (2 counted sources, 30154 views). Nearest destination: none proposed; Haʻapai has only 3 kept spots, below the four-spot bar. Reached by chartered boat from Pangai, ~80 km west, so standalone.

name: Uoleva
note: Kept (2 counted sources, 813 views). Standalone: no Haʻapai destination (only 3 kept spots).

name: Neiafu

name: Niuatoputapu

name: Tafahi
note: Separate island reached by boat from Niuatoputapu; own journey; standalone.
